note: deadCount is the site-level tally (tooling/control-census.mjs totals.dead) — every control instance (menu item or button) whose dispatched action was invoked while available and produced no observable effect, threw, logged an error, or was never registered. distinctDeadActions is the same defect set counted once per underlying command instead of once per button/menu site; see this run's evidence report for the full grouped list. Lower either only by fixing real wiring, not by narrowing what the census walks.
_note: Lowered after open-model-settings was registered: one wire, twenty-six sites.
_note2: lane-edit, 2026-09-01: -43 sites / -3 distinct actions (367->324, 146->143). copy (17 sites) and cut (13 sites) silently no-op'd with an editable field focused but nothing selected — isAvailable() checked hasEditableFocus, not an actual selection; now gated on a real non-collapsed selection (hasEditableSelectionRange in window-manager.js) and given the same setStatus receipt the Markdown-export copy path already uses (copied_selection/cut_selection), so a real copy/cut is no longer invisible to the census's DOM diff. clear-edit (13 sites) had the same availability bug PLUS a worse one: with no selection, document.execCommand('delete') silently deleted one unselected character next to the caret — an unrequested edit, not a no-op; the same selection gate removes the whole class. All three are wired into balloonHelpSelectionRequiredActions so the menu item greys out with a real reason instead of looking clickable and doing nothing. NOT counted here (verified genuinely live by direct clipboard/activeElement/status reproduction, code already correct, no product fix made): select-all (16 sites) and focus-search-query (1 site) change selectionStart/end or document.activeElement, neither of which the census's snapshot() tracks; find-change-current (1) and find-change-next (4) already say 'Type the text to find.' / 'No match for ...' / 'Match N of M.' correctly, but the census processes find-change-all/current/next back to back alphabetically and each begins its probe from an empty query, so consecutive dispatches emit the identical status string and the diff sees no change — a harness artifact (alphabetical adjacency + shared empty-query message), not a product defect. Left the baseline honest rather than lowering it on an unverifiable rerun; flagged the census harness gap as a separate follow-up.
_note3: lane-dead-controls-3, 2026-09-02: -66 sites / -68 distinct actions (124->58, 90->22), measured against the two parked commits this lane resumed (e8415e8c, 0225e9a6). One defect class did most of it: a menu row that names one of a set of alternatives carried no mark, so the choice already in force looked the same as the others and choosing it changed the app and told nobody. Six sets were given the mark their own module already knew -- ClioChart projections, ClioPaint tools and the filled-shape switch, CMF Studio views, Micropolis speeds, Bonsai City speeds -- through a data-* key on the row plus a branch in updateMenuState() that asks the module which one it holds; an unloaded module answers with nothing, so the rows stay unmarked rather than claiming a default. Each setter now calls updateMenuState() so the mark moves with the choice. The two game speed sets carried a second defect underneath: with no city loaded they set a field on an absent simulation, so they are now unavailable and grey with a stated reason instead of black and silent. Verified in the running app at 127.0.0.1:4230 by clicking each row and reading the mark back: ClioChart bars->matrix, ClioPaint pencil->oval and the filled toggle, CMF back->front, and the four Bonsai speed rows disabled with balloon_disabled_menu_context while no city is loaded.
_note4: lane-dead-controls-3, 2026-09-02, second pass: -33 sites / -16 distinct actions (58->25, 22->6). Three product repairs and four widenings of what the walk can see, each checked by hand in the running app before it was written. PRODUCT: ClioChart's Reverse Sort greyed out, with a stated reason, when the table has fewer than two measured objects in the column in force -- on a blank template it flipped a flag, repainted the same unmeasured rows and said nothing (1 site). ClioPaint's New says 'This picture is already new. Nothing to clear.' instead of repeating the sentence the window shows from the moment it opens (2 sites). ClioTalk's Open Recent marks the conversation the viewer is showing, so the row for what is already open no longer reads like every other row (1 site). TOOLING (see the commit 'Control census: four things the walk could not see'): the status line is wiped before each dispatch, because the walk visits ids alphabetically and two neighbours answering with the same sentence made the second one look mute -- this is what freed the eight ai-* writing tools, which all answer through beginLongTask's one receipt; a selection range is read from the focused field and from the document, for Select All; clicks on file inputs are counted, for the three Cover Glass Choose... commands that hand the question to the operating system; and a row that names one of a set of alternatives, chosen while it is already in force, is read as inert rather than dead, because the check mark says so -- applied only after the command has run, only to the bare no-op reading, and only to a row with a sibling carrying the same choice key, so a lone toggle is still measured the ordinary way.
_note5: lane-dead-controls-3, 2026-09-03, third pass: -23 sites / -4 distinct actions (25->2, 6->2). PRODUCT: select-all (16 sites) was the largest single defect left in the app and it was real, not a blind spot -- in an empty field select() moves the caret from 0-0 to 0-0, so the row was black in sixteen menus and did nothing in all of them; it is now gated on hasEditableText, the same correction Cut/Copy/Clear already carry, and greys out saying the field is empty. The two eli5 section commands (3 sites each) are offered from Section Drafts and nowhere else, and every answer they gave went into Quick Draft's own status bar, a window the writer is not looking at; both now announce through one helper that repeats the message in the system status line whenever Quick Draft is not the window in front. Closing the only Time Machine tab (1 site) lands on the home panel, which is what the window already showed, so it now says 'Tab closed.' TOOLING: both field readings in the snapshot stopped at sixty elements while this walk leaves seventy-six windows open, so the sixty could all belong to windows nobody is looking at; the front window's fields are read first and the cap falls on the rest.
_open: Two commands, two sites, both understood and neither repaired here. ai-praise at the Review Desk: it runs, writes 'Writing encouragement...', gets its answer from the model, appends it to the Review Desk body and then calls clearStatus(), so within the probe's own window the status it wrote is gone again and the text it added lives in a textarea. Not a wiring defect -- a receipt that erases itself. open-chat-file: the row now carries the mark for the conversation the viewer is showing, and the walk probes it in the state where that conversation is already the one open, so the command is asked for what is already true; the already-in-force rule does not catch it because the mark is computed from the viewer's own state rather than from a shared choice key. Both were live in one of the four runs this lane made and dead in another, so both are state-dependent. Neither should be lowered further without deciding, deliberately, what a self-erasing receipt is worth.
_reconciled: Five lanes lowered this from one 367/146 baseline over disjoint sets: edit commands -43 sites/-3 actions, the writing-tool cluster -126/-16, games -2/-2, creative labs -11/-11, and the desk cluster -61/-24. Repairs whose effect the census cannot yet observe -- a ticker line, an engine field, a canvas paint, a selection, a focus move -- are deliberately NOT credited and stay counted as dead until the census tooling can see them, so this number is conservative by construction.
